proposal: dual electric/magnetic dipole force with omitted coherent outgoing recoil
decision: Scientifically sound, but this is the same apparatus/calibration loophole/physical correction as the archived dipole-recoil family. Arbitrary incident gradients or Lorentz response dispersion would broaden the supplied mathematics without creating a distinct missing physical mechanism.

shared_background_and_distinction.retained_electric_dipole_force: The retained task tests incoming electric canonical momentum versus total Poynting momentum, with no magnetic response or electric-magnetic recoil. The proposed task would be distinct from that retained task.
shared_background_and_distinction.archived_dipole_recoil: Already supplies radiatively dressed electric and magnetic polarizabilities, fits a common scale from both isolated-channel preparations, and omits only outgoing coherent interference momentum. This matches the new proposal.

conventions.response: p=alpha_e E_inc; m=alpha_m H_inc; no magnetoelectric response
conventions.incoming_force: F_i=.5 Re[sum_j p_j* partial_i E_j + m_j* partial_i H_j]
conventions.far_field: r E_sc exp(-ikr)=k^2/(4 pi) [p-n(n dot p)+m cross n]
conventions.power_density: dP/dOmega=k^4/(32 pi^2) |p-n(n dot p)+m cross n|^2
conventions.integral_identities: Total radiated power=k^4/(12 pi)(|p|^2+|m|^2); radiated momentum=k^4/(12 pi) Re[p cross m*]. The electric/magnetic cross term integrates to zero power, but nonzero momentum.
conventions.passivity: For alpha=a/(1-i k^3 a/(6 pi)) and real a, Im alpha=k^3|alpha|^2/(6 pi); the existing model obeys the lossless optical theorem.
conventions.primary_source_unit_conversion: The cited arXiv source uses unrationalized polarizabilities; its radiation dressing coefficient2/3 becomes1/(6 pi) after the4 pi polarizability conversion. The archived rationalized reference independently fixes the normalization.

primary_sources.title: Optical forces on small magnetodielectric particles
primary_sources.support: Generic incident-field force decomposes into electric, magnetic and electric-magnetic scattered-momentum contributions.

primary_sources.title: Electric and magnetic dipolar response of Germanium spheres: Interference effects, scattering anisotropy and optical forces
primary_sources.support: Equations6–9 give radiative response and angular scattering; section3 gives interference recoil. Its equal-response limit halves the force relative to summed isolated channels while preserving total scattered power.

existing_outcome.plain_failures: One reviewed physical failure; two physical passes. All original evidence retained.
